paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as Rabbah bar Shmuel. See the parallel [entry in Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3148&lang=en). He lists appearances under the name Abba bar Shmuel in [Bava Batra 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.15b.14), Eruvin 13b according to Dikdukei Soferim (compare the [current Talmud text](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.13b.10)), [Zevachim 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.105a.14), and Sanhedrin, chapter 3, under the printed marker ה״מ (compare [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:9:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.3.9.19)).[^4][^5]

notes.text: The printed Sanhedrin halakhah marker ה״מ is unresolved. Hyman’s identification with Rabbah bar Shmuel is reported without changing authority records.

The supplied Sanhedrin marker ה״מ remains unresolved. Earlier whole-chapter and finite-search nonmatch reports are inherited research claims, not a fresh inspection or universal absence proof; shorter בא was only an untested lead. Hyman owns the Abba/Rabbah identification and the Dikdukei Soferim variant. The headword’s abbreviated title is retained as R' without borrowing a full title from a different occurrence or familiar figure.

The consulted Bava Batra 15b and Zevachim 105a both name Rabbi Abba bar Shmuel. In Eruvin 13b the consulted Talmud text has Rabbi Abba speaking in Shmuel’s name. Rabbinovicz’s Dikdukei Soferim on Eruvin (Munich, 1873, Google Books image 39) gives Abba [bar] Shmuel in its manuscript column alongside the printed reading. Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 55) gives ה״מ after Sanhedrin chapter 3. The passage intended by that marker remains unresolved.

[Eruvin 13b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.13b.10) reads “Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel.” The [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3148&lang=en) also directs readers to Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin. The consulted [Sanhedrin passage](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.3.9.19) has Ba (bar) Shmuel, with “bar” in parentheses, while Guggenheimer translates it as a transmission in Shmuel’s name. Hyman’s exact printed marker remains uncertain.

The printed column reads “Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel.” The manuscript column records Abba [bar] Shmuel. See the [printed Dikdukei Soferim apparatus](https://books.google.com/books?id=-tMwzyO-dBEC&pg=PA39).
